title: The Ninth Proof
description: A scholar has vanished from the University of Thepyrgos, leaving behind a notebook filled with diagrams of a forbidden game called Kon'reh. The Ninth Proof is a mathematical demonstration that reality is a board — and completing it could unmake the boundaries between what is and what could be. The party must navigate the war between the Witness's Archivists and the Ninth's Coterie, rescue the missing scholar, and decide the fate of the proof itself.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: The Hollow Bride
bestiary.description: A manifestation of the Ninth, appearing when the proof is near completion. She offers bargains that seem fair — but she collects her price in names, memories, and promises. Her voice is honey and razors.

sb_spends.name: Whisper of Honey
sb_spends.effect: Target gains a Boon but marks 1 Obligation to the Ninth.

sb_spends.name: Razor's Edge
sb_spends.effect: Target must answer a question truthfully or take Harm 1 (Mental).

sb_spends.name: The Ninth's Bargain
sb_spends.effect: Target is bound by a geas until they complete a task. Breaking it costs 1 Corruption.

bestiary.weakness: Cannot cross a line of salt. Cannot harm those who speak a true regret aloud.

bestiary.name: The Voice of the Ninth
bestiary.description: The leader of the Ninth's Coterie. Speaks in paradoxes. Offers bargains that seem reasonable — but every bargain erases a memory.

sb_spends.name: Bargain of Forgetting
sb_spends.effect: Target gains +1 die for the scene but loses a minor memory (GM chooses).

sb_spends.name: The Ninth's Authority
sb_spends.effect: Target must obey one command or take Harm 2 (Mental).

bestiary.name: Paper Wraith
bestiary.description: Ninth-created entities that erase knowledge and memories. They appear in the archives when the proof is disturbed.

sb_spends.name: Memory Drain
sb_spends.effect: Target loses a minor memory (a face, a name, a place).

sb_spends.name: Ink Blot
sb_spends.effect: A document or book is erased, becoming unreadable.

sb_spends.name: Erasure
sb_spends.effect: Target loses one skill die for the scene.

bestiary.name: Archive Guardian
bestiary.description: Witness-created constructs that preserve and protect the archives. They attack intruders with precision and silence.

sb_spends.name: Silent Alarm
sb_spends.effect: Summon 1d4 additional guardians; ticks Witness's Vigil +1.

bestiary.name: Echo Scholar
bestiary.description: A scholar who has been partially consumed by the Ninth's influence. They speak in half-remembered truths and offer dangerous knowledge.

sb_spends.name: Fragmented Truth
sb_spends.effect: Reveal a clue, but the scholar gains 1 Obligation on the recipient.

sb_spends.name: Echo of Memory
sb_spends.effect: The scholar remembers a name. That name is now a target for the Ninth.

acts.title: The Game Awakens
acts.description: The party investigates Lerris's disappearance, discovering the Kon'reh notebook and the secret society of scholars who play it. They must navigate the University's politics while the game begins to reveal its true nature.

scenes.title: The Missing Scholar
scenes.description: Markus Fenwood, Lerris's brother, is desperate. He has found a notebook in Lerris's quarters filled with cryptic diagrams. The last entry reads: 'The Ninth Rim opens at the salt-pressed hour. I will count to eight and leave the ninth for the door.'

timers.name: Lerris's Fate
timers.description: How close Lerris is to being lost to the game

timers.name: Hollow Attention
timers.description: How much the Hollow has noticed the party

outcomes.clean: You decode the notebook's basic structure — Kon'reh is a game of encirclement and escape, but the diagrams suggest something more: a proof that rewrites the rules of the board.
outcomes.partial: You understand the game's surface, but the deeper meaning eludes you. The GM gains 1 SB to use on a 'Ninth Rim' complication.
outcomes.miss: You misread a diagram; the Hollow notices. Tick Hollow Attention +1 and the GM gains 2 SB.

scenes.title: The Game Begins
scenes.description: The party is approached by a scholar from the Ninth's Coterie. They offer a deal: help them complete the proof, and they will reveal Lerris's location. But their offer is a trap — the proof requires a sacrifice.

timers.name: Ninth's Progress
timers.description: How close the Coterie is to completing the proof

timers.name: Witness's Vigil
timers.description: How close the Archivists are to seizing the proof

outcomes.clean: You extract information without committing. You learn that Lerris is being held in the Sunken Archive — a forbidden section of the University sealed by the Witness.
outcomes.partial: You learn Lerris's location, but you owe the Coterie a favor. Mark 1 Obligation to the Ninth.
outcomes.miss: You accept a poisoned deal. Tick Ninth's Progress +2. The Coterie now has leverage over you.

scenes.title: The Sunken Archive
scenes.description: The archive is a labyrinth of forbidden texts, sealed by the Witness's Archivists. It is here that Lerris is being held — and where the Kon'reh board is being assembled. The party must infiltrate the archive and rescue Lerris before the proof is completed.

outcomes.clean: You reach Lerris. He is alive, but changed — he has been playing Kon'reh for days, and the game has begun to affect his mind. He mutters: 'The ninth rim is not a rule. It is a door. The Hollow answered.'
outcomes.partial: You find Lerris, but the Archivists are alerted. You must escape through the Whispering Gallery.
outcomes.miss: You are caught. The Archivists detain you. Tick Witness's Vigil +2.

outcomes.clean: You defeat the guardians and escape with Lerris.
outcomes.partial: You escape, but one guardian follows. It will appear again at a critical moment.
outcomes.miss: You are overwhelmed. Tick Witness's Vigil +2 and mark 1 Fatigue for each PC.

acts.title: The Ninth Rim
acts.description: Lerris is free, but the game is already in motion. The party must learn the true nature of Kon'reh, navigate the war between the Witness and the Ninth, and decide which faction — if any — to support.

scenes.title: Lerris's Revelation
scenes.description: Lerris explains: Kon'reh is not just a game. It is a proof — a mathematical demonstration that reality is a board. The ninth rim is the edge of the board. Those who cross it can rewrite the rules of existence. The proof is almost complete. The Coterie wants to complete it. The Witness wants to seal it.

outcomes.clean: You fully understand the proof's nature. You gain +1 die on all rolls involving Kon'reh for the rest of the adventure.
outcomes.partial: You understand the basics, but the deeper implications elude you. The GM may spend 1 SB to confuse a key detail.
outcomes.miss: Lerris's explanation is fragmented by fear. You gain the condition 'Haunted by the Ninth' (-1 die to Resolve tests).

scenes.title: The Archivists' Demand
scenes.description: The Witness's Archivists arrive. They demand that the party hand over the Kon'reh notebook and any fragments of the proof. They offer protection in exchange. But their protection is a cage — they will seal the knowledge away, and Lerris with it.

outcomes.clean: You convince the Archivists to share information without surrendering the notebook. You learn that the proof was originally discovered by Aqyl the Elder — and that he sealed it for a reason.
outcomes.partial: You negotiate a compromise: you will share the proof, but you keep the original. The Archivists agree — but they will watch you closely.
outcomes.miss: The Archivists seize the notebook. Tick Witness's Vigil +2. You must recover it.

scenes.title: The Game Board
scenes.description: The Coterie has assembled the Kon'reh board in a hidden chamber beneath the University. The board is not a game — it is a prayer. Each piece is a name. Each move is a memory. The final move — the Ninth Proof — will be played at the next salt-pressed hour.

outcomes.clean: You understand the board's true nature. You may attempt to sabotage the proof (requires a Craft or Lore test, DV 5).
outcomes.partial: You gain a clue about the proof's weakness, but the Coterie notices your presence. Tick Ninth's Progress +1.
outcomes.miss: The board speaks to you. Tick Hollow Attention +2. You now know the name of the final piece — and it is yours.

acts.title: The Final Proof
acts.description: The salt-pressed hour approaches. The party must decide the fate of the Ninth Proof: complete it, seal it, or destroy it. The Hollow is watching. The Ninth is waiting. And the game is almost over.

scenes.title: The Salt-Pressed Hour
scenes.description: The Coterie is gathered in the chamber beneath the University. The board is complete. The salt ring glows. The Hollow watches. The Ninth Proof is one move away. The party must act now — or the door will open.

outcomes.clean: You resist her influence and make your choice freely. The party gains +1 die on the final resolution roll.
outcomes.partial: You resist, but the Hollow Bride claims a memory from each PC. Mark 1 Fatigue.
outcomes.miss: You accept a bargain. The Hollow Bride claims a name from the party. Mark 1 Corruption.

outcomes.clean: You resolve the proof on your terms. See Resolution Paths below.
outcomes.partial: You resolve the proof, but at a cost. The Hollow gains a foothold. Tick Hollow Attention to 0 — but the party is marked.
outcomes.miss: The proof is completed. The door opens. The Ninth Proof is played. Reality rewrites itself. The party must escape.

scenes.title: Resolution Paths
scenes.description: The party has four options — each with lasting consequences.

outcomes.clean: The Ninth Proof is played. Reality rewrites itself. The party gains immense knowledge — but the Hollow gains a foothold in the world. Lerris is lost to the game. Award 18-20 XP. Gain a permanent connection to the Ninth.
outcomes.partial: The proof is partially completed. The party gains some knowledge, but the Hollow's influence spreads. Award 12-15 XP.
outcomes.miss: The proof is completed, but the party is caught in the backlash. All PCs mark 1 Corruption.

outcomes.clean: The party aligns with the Witness's Archivists. The proof is sealed away — but the knowledge is lost. The Coterie is destroyed. Award 12-15 XP. Gain a permanent connection to the Witness.
outcomes.partial: The proof is sealed, but some fragments survive. The Ninth's influence lingers. Award 8-10 XP.
outcomes.miss: The sealing fails. The proof is lost, and the Archivists blame the party. Gain a Black Mark with the Witness.

outcomes.clean: The party destroys the board and the notebook. The proof is lost forever. The Ninth's Coterie is shattered. Award 10-12 XP. Gain a permanent enemy in the Ninth's Coterie.
outcomes.partial: The board is destroyed, but the notebook survives. The Coterie will return. Award 8-10 XP.
outcomes.miss: The destruction fails. The proof is completed. The party must flee.

outcomes.clean: The party negotiates with the Ninth itself. The proof is not completed, but the Ninth is appeased. Award 15-18 XP. Gain a Ninth's Boon (once per session, reroll any roll). The party is forever marked by the Hollow.
outcomes.partial: The bargain is struck, but the price is steep. Each PC loses a memory. Award 10-12 XP.
outcomes.miss: The Ninth refuses the bargain. The proof is completed. The party must flee.

npcs.secret: Haunted by his father's Concordance. Fears the Hollow more than he admits.

npcs.name: Lerris Fenwood
npcs.secret: He believes the proof will set him free. He is wrong.

npcs.role: Tutor, Keeper of the Salt-Pressed Leaves

npcs.motivation: Seal the proof, protect the University

locations.name: Lerris's Study
locations.description: A cramped room in the University's north wing. The walls are covered in Kon'reh diagrams. The salt ring on the desk is still damp.

locations.name: The Sunken Archive
locations.description: A sealed section of the Library of Keys. The books here are forbidden. The Archivists guard them with their lives — and their silence.

locations.name: The Salt-Pressed Chamber
locations.description: A hidden room beneath the University. The floor is a Kon'reh board. The walls are lined with names. The air tastes of salt and old promises.

locations.name: The Archivolt
locations.description: The main hall of the Library of Keys. The Witness's Archivists hold court here. The books whisper truths — and lies.

locations.name: The Ninth Rim
locations.description: The outermost edge of the Kon'reh board. To cross it is to leave the game. The party may be forced to cross — or to prevent others from doing so.

factions.name: Markus Fenwood
factions.relationship: The party's first contact and a moral compass. Desperate, loyal, and willing to bend the rules.

factions.name: The Ninth's Coterie
factions.relationship: They believe the Ninth will bring liberation — but the Ninth only brings forgetting. Their leader is the Voice of the Ninth.

factions.name: The Witness's Archivists
factions.goals: Seal the proof and protect the University
factions.relationship: They believe knowledge must be preserved and protected. They are willing to sacrifice Lerris to keep the proof hidden.

factions.name: Aqyl, Son of Aqyl
factions.goals: Preserve the truth for the right time
factions.relationship: Keeper of the Salt-Pressed Leaves. Knows the proof's true nature. Speaks only when asked thrice.

factions.name: The Hollow
factions.goals: Watch and wait for the door to open
factions.relationship: Not a faction, but a pressure. Patient, hungry, and eternal. It watches the proof. It waits for the door to open.

campaignTimers.name: Lerris's Fate
campaignTimers.description: How close Lerris is to being lost to the game. Advances when the party delays, when the Coterie completes a move, or when the party ignores a clue. When full, Lerris becomes the final piece — the Ninth Proof is played.

campaignTimers.name: Ninth's Progress
campaignTimers.description: How close the Ninth's Coterie is to completing the proof. Advances when the party accepts Coterie bargains, fails to stop a move, or ignores a warning. When full, the Ninth Proof is complete — the door opens.

campaignTimers.name: Witness's Vigil
campaignTimers.description: How close the Witness's Archivists are to seizing the proof. Advances when the party aids the Coterie, avoids the Archivists, or breaks archive rules. When full, the Archivists raid the party's safehouse and seize the notebook.

campaignTimers.name: Hollow Attention
campaignTimers.description: How much the Hollow has noticed the party's involvement. Advances when the party speaks names, completes moves, or lingers in sealed chambers. When full, the Hollow Bride appears — offering a bargain, demanding a price.

notes: A cosmic horror investigation set in the University of Thepyrgos. The party must navigate the war between the Witness and the Ninth while a forbidden game threatens to rewrite reality. Themes: the price of knowledge, the Hollow's attention, and the nature of proof. Inspired by Kon'reh: The Ninth Rim.

_gmhints.tone: THIS ADVENTURE IS A SERIOUS, BROODING COSMIC HORROR INVESTIGATION. The tone should be tense, academic, and unsettling—like a slow-burn horror story set in a university archive. The Ninth Proof is not a game to be won; it is a door to be closed. The Hollow Bride is a figure of folklore—when she appears, she should feel wildly out of place, like a fairy tale intruding on a rationalist's nightmare. Markus is cautious, broken, and seeking new purpose in saving his brother—play his desperation with restraint. Lerris is hopelessly naive, adventurous, and wry in Act I—his transformation into a haunted monster hunter is far in the future, so for now he is bright-eyed and dangerously curious. The University of Thepyrgos should feel ancient, labyrinthine, and indifferent to human suffering. The Archivists are not villains—they are custodians of a burden too heavy for most to carry. The Coterie are not heroes—they are dreamers who have forgotten that dreams can be nightmares.

pacing.act1: Act I is about investigation and the slow realization that something is very wrong. Markus is the emotional core—his desperation is quiet, not loud. Lerris's disappearance should feel like a mystery, not a rescue mission. The Kon'reh notebook is a puzzle—let the party decode it piece by piece. The Coterie's offer should feel seductive and dangerous, not obviously evil. The Hollow Attention timer advances when the party speaks names or reads forbidden texts—describe it as 'a cold draft' or 'a whisper from the corner of the room.' The Sunken Archive is a labyrinth of forgotten knowledge—emphasize the weight of the books, the silence of the Archivists, the sense that the University has forgotten its own secrets.
pacing.act2: Act II is about understanding the stakes. Lerris is free, but he is changed—he has been playing Kon'reh for days, and the game has begun to affect his mind. His explanation of the proof should be fragmented and urgent. The Archivists' demand is a test of loyalty—they offer protection, but their protection is a cage. The Game Board scene is the horror reveal: the board is not a game, it is a prayer. Each piece is a name. Each move is a memory. The Ninth Proof is almost complete. The Hollow Attention timer is now a tangible threat—describe the Hollow as 'something watching from the space between words.'
pacing.act3: Act III is the climax. The salt-pressed hour approaches. The Hollow Bride appears—she is a figure of folklore, so she should feel like she has stepped out of a different story entirely. She is honey and razors, beautiful and wrong. The Final Choice is not a combat—it is a philosophical reckoning. Let the party debate. Let them feel the weight of their decision. The resolution paths are not 'good' and 'bad'—they are all costs. Lerris's fate is tied to the proof; if it is completed, he is lost to the game. If it is sealed, he survives but is forever haunted. If it is destroyed, he is free but the knowledge is gone forever. The Ninth's Bargain is the tragic path—the proof is not completed, but the party is marked. Play all outcomes with gravity and sorrow.

npcSecrets.markus-fenwood: Markus is cautious, broken, and seeking new purpose. He is not a hero—he is a man who has failed before and fears failing again. His father's Concordance haunts him—he will not speak of it unless pressed. He is loyal to Lerris, but his loyalty is tinged with guilt. Play him as restrained, watchful, and quietly desperate. His arc is about finding purpose in helping his brother—not about saving the world.
npcSecrets.lerris-fenwood: Lerris is hopelessly naive, adventurous, and wry. He genuinely believes the proof will set him free—he does not understand what he is playing with. In Act I, he is bright-eyed and curious. In Act II, he is changed—haunted by what he has seen. In Act III, he may be lost to the game entirely. His transformation into a haunted monster hunter is far in the future—do not foreshadow it heavily; let it be a tragic possibility, not an inevitability. He is not the hero; he is the victim who might become something else.
npcSecrets.aqyl-son-of-aqyl: He knows the proof's true nature. He will not speak of it unless asked thrice—this is not a game; it is a test of sincerity. He is the keeper of knowledge that is too dangerous to share freely. He is not withholding to be cruel—he is withholding because the truth is a burden.
npcSecrets.voice-of-the-ninth: She speaks in paradoxes. She offers bargains that seem fair—but every bargain erases a memory. She is not evil; she is a function of the Ninth. She remembers every name spoken in her presence. She is patient. She is waiting.
npcSecrets.keeper-lian: She has not spoken aloud in twenty years. She writes on water. Her silence is a judgment. She is not cold—she is burdened by the weight of what she knows. She will help the party if they prove worthy of the truth.
npcSecrets.hollow-bride: She is a figure of folklore—the Hollow Bride appears in stories told to children, a cautionary tale about bargains and promises. When she appears in this adventure, she should feel wildly out of place—like a fairy tale intruding on a rationalist's nightmare. She is not a monster to be fought; she is a presence to be negotiated with. Her voice is honey and razors. She will offer a bargain—and collect the price.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: That the Ninth Proof is a door to another reality — hint at it, but do not state it plainly until Act II
That Lerris is a willing participant in the Coterie — this is an Act II reveal; in Act I, he is a victim
That the Hollow Bride is a folklore figure who should feel out of place — let this realization dawn slowly
That the Witness's Archivists are willing to sacrifice Lerris — this is the moral gut-punch of Act II; do not foreshadow it heavily
That Aqyl will only speak when asked thrice — this is a puzzle to solve, not a handout
That the Ninth's Bargain path results in the party being marked — this is a consequence, not a selling point

cosmicHorrorTactics.atmosphere: Describe the University as ancient, labyrinthine, and indifferent. The books whisper. The Archivists move in silence. The air tastes of salt and old promises. The Hollow's presence is felt as a cold draft, a whisper from the corner of the room, a name spoken just out of earshot.
cosmicHorrorTactics.konreh_revelations: The Kon'reh board is not a game—it is a prayer. Each piece is a name. Each move is a memory. When the party sees the board, describe it as 'wrong'—like a map of a place that cannot exist. The diagrams should be beautiful and unsettling.
cosmicHorrorTactics.hollow_bride_entrance: The Hollow Bride is a figure of folklore—she should feel like she has stepped out of a different story. Her entrance should be jarring: a wedding dress in a dusty archive, a voice that sounds like a lullaby, a smile that does not reach her eyes. She is not evil—she is an intrusion, a reality fracture made manifest.
cosmicHorrorTactics.markus_tension: Markus is cautious and broken. He will not charge in—he will plan, hesitate, and second-guess. Let his caution be a source of tension: he wants to save Lerris, but he is terrified of failing. His arc is about finding the courage to act despite his fear.
cosmicHorrorTactics.lerris_naivety: Lerris is hopelessly naive in Act I—he believes the proof will set him free. Let him be charming and optimistic, even as the evidence mounts that he is wrong. His transformation is far in the future—for now, he is a victim who does not know he needs saving.
cosmicHorrorTactics.the_cost: Every choice has a cost. The party will lose something—a memory, a name, a promise. Emphasize the weight of these losses. The Ninth Proof is not a game to be won; it is a door to be closed. The victory is in the closing, not the opening.
